text:
The number of Fubini rankings (i.e. parking functions) that give a prescribed parking outcome π is  

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
\prod_{i=1}^{n}\Bigl(i-
\bigl|\{\,j<i : \pi^{-1}(j) > \pi^{-1}(i)\,\}\bigr|\Bigr)
}
\]

where \(\pi^{-1}(i)\) is the spot occupied by car \(i\) in the outcome, and the factor for each \(i\) subtracts the number of earlier‑arriving cars that end up to the **right** of car \(i\) (i.e. the inversions \((j,i)\) with \(j<i\)).  

For a permutation that has exactly \(k\) ascending runs, this product depends only on the pattern of those runs; in particular it equals \(n!\) when \(k=1\) (the identity outcome) and equals 1 when \(k=n\) (the completely decreasing outcome).  

**ANSWER:** \(\displaystyle \prod_{i=1}^{n}\Bigl(i-
|\{j<i : \pi^{-1}(j) > \pi^{-1}(i)\}|\Bigr)\)
